notes.text:
This update for cyrus-sasl fixes the following issues:

Security issue fixed:

- CVE-2026-107161: Heap buffer overflow in cyrus-sasl add_to_challenge() allows malicious server to crash or compromise
  DIGEST-MD5 clients (bsc#1284687).

Non security issues fixed:

- Fix cyrus-sasl package failing to build with GCC 14 (bsc#1221863).
- Replace insecure MD5 with ephemeral HMAC-SHA256 (bsc#1247498).
- Make DIGEST-MD5 work with openssl3 (bsc#1230111).

notes.text: A heap-based buffer overflow flaw was found in Cyrus SASL. The add_to_challenge() function in the DIGEST-MD5 plugin computes the size of the buffer needed for a challenge/response field before DIGEST-MD5 quoting is applied, but does not recompute that size when quoting (escaping special characters) makes the value longer. The under-sized buffer is then passed to strcat(), causing a heap-based out-of-bounds write whose size depends on attacker-controlled input. A malicious or on-path DIGEST-MD5 (or HTTP Digest) server can trigger this flaw in a connecting client by supplying a crafted challenge field, such as realm or nonce, most likely resulting in a crash of the client application.
